65.0.0.en: 1 “I gave ear to them that asked not for me; I was found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.

65.0.1.en: “I gave ear to them that asked not for me; I was found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name” [1]. It is clear here that the discourse concerns the acceptance of the Gentiles, who had not known God nor sought Him before nor borne His name, but who believed in the Savior and so enjoyed what the people of God had deprived themselves of.

65.0.2.en: St. Paul spoke of the calling of the Gentiles and the rejection of the unbelieving Jews in his Epistle to the Romans (Rom 9:11), citing the prophetic statement found here (Rom 10:20-21). For God gave ear to the Gentiles who had not asked Him, and those who had not sought Him found Him, because while we were enemies He reconciled us to the Father. He loved all mankind before they loved Him, and chose us before we knew Him or sought Him. He inclined our hearts to Himself, taking the initiative of love before His name was called upon us.

65.0.3.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [Did Israel hear and not understand? If the pagan Gentiles have heard and grasped the faith, how much more should the Jews have done, to whom God gave from of old all the signs aimed at removing the veil from their eyes].

65.0.4.en: * Who are those who did not seek Him? Who are those who did not ask for Him? Certainly not the Jews, but those who are of the Gentiles who did not know Him, whom Moses described in the words: “not a people,” “a foolish nation”; and on the same basis he refers to them here because of their extreme ignorance.

65.0.5.en: It is a very great shame that those who did not seek Him found Him, and those who searched for Him lost Him (through their unbelief).

65.0.6.en: St. John Chrysostom * Who is this who was revealed (and whom the Gentiles found) but the Word of the Father, when the Father sent Him, and in Him is the power for men that proceeds from Him?!

65.1.0.en: 2 I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts; 3 A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick; 4 Which remain among the graves, and lodge in the monuments, which eat swine's flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels; 5 Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day. 6 Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, even recompense into their bosom, 7 Your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, saith the LORD, which have burned incense upon the mountains, and blasphemed me upon the hills: therefore will I measure their former work into their bosom.”

65.1.1.en: “I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts.” The Lord spread out His hands on the Cross with love to embrace all and give them the life of victory, as the prophet Moses spread out his hands during the battle against Amalek, as a symbol of the saving work of Christ.

65.1.2.en: The Lord spread out His hands from His side, waiting for us to respond to this work by seeking Him every day, as St. Paphnutius says.

65.1.3.en: As for the secret of God's rejection of His people, it is:

65.1.4.en: a. Their rebellion [2], seeking to walk according to their own desires and not according to the mind of God.

65.2.0.en: b. Their breaking of the Law, and their turning aside to idolatrous worship [3-4].

65.3.1.en: St. Augustine sees that the denial of faith in the Lord is death, for they saw the miracles of the Savior with their own eyes and did not live through them, but remained as in a state of death.

65.4.0.en: 8 Thus saith the LORD, “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all. 9 And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains: and mine elect shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there. 10 And Sharon shall be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for the herds to lie down in, for my people that have sought me.”

65.4.1.en: Although the people as a whole took a stand of ingratitude, there is a holy remnant for the Lord, such as the disciples, the Apostles, the Marys, Zacchaeus the tax collector, Levi, and so on... This holy few does not perish but is a blessing. “Thus saith the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all” [8].

65.5.0.en: Among the opponents there were found those chosen by the Lord, His servants, who seek Him [10].

65.6.s.en: 4. A comparison between the believers and the unbelievers:

65.6.0.en: 11 “But ye are they that forsake the LORD, that forget my holy mountain, that prepare a table for the Greater Fortune, and that fill mixed wine for the Lesser Fortune. 12 Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down to the slaughter: because when I called, ye did not answer; when I spake, ye did not hear; but did evil before mine eyes, and did choose that wherein I delighted not. 13 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: 14 Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit. 15 And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen: for the Lord GOD shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name: 16 That he who blesseth himself in the earth shall bless himself in the God of truth; and he that sweareth in the earth shall swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hid from mine eyes.”

65.6.1.en: a. Some of those who forsook the Lord thought that they would be saved by holding idolatrous feasts marked by luxury and drunkenness, and they did not realize that they had become like sheep for the slaughter [11-12].

65.7.0.en: b. The unbelievers often think that they live in luxury without deprivation, but soon the believers are satisfied and the unbelievers hunger, the former rejoice and the latter grieve. The believers enjoy a life of praise and inner rejoicing while the hearts of the unbelievers are broken [13-15].

65.8.0.en: c. The believers are exposed to afflictions, but they receive the blessing of the true God even while on earth, and so they forget their troubles amid God's consolations and His blessing [16].

65.9.s.en: 5. The new heavens and the new earth:

65.9.0.en: 17 “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind. 18 But be ye glad and rejoice for ever in that which I create: for, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy. 19 And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people: and the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying. 20 There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed. 21 And they shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them. 22 They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands. 23 They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth for terror; for they are the seed of the blessed of the LORD, and their offspring with them. 24 And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear. 25 The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD.”

65.9.1.en: The prophet Isaiah presents to us a wonderful picture of the work of the Lord Christ the Creator in establishing the Church of the New Testament. He created new heavens and a new earth [17]; He established a true renewal of the soul (the heavens) and of the body (the earth), so that soul and body together came into harmony, since both submitted to His Holy Spirit. The old conflict between the desires of the soul and the desires of the body has ended, and by the Holy Spirit we have entered into a life of spiritual joy and heavenly gladness, as our life is filled with the fruit of the Holy Spirit, love, joy and peace (Gal 5:22). We rejoice, as a holy bride renewed by her Bridegroom, and He rejoices in us, for He says: “And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people” [19]. It is the joy of mutual love!

65.9.2.en: In this new life that became ours in Baptism, wolves are turned into lambs, so the wolf feeds with the lamb, and the nature of predation and ferocity is shattered, so the lion eats with the ox. As for the serpents, they do not hurt nor destroy the one who knows his sonship to God and lives by the possibilities of the life that has become his].

65.9.3.en: The marks of this new life are:

65.9.4.en: a. We no longer remember the former life, nor does it come into our mind, because the overflow of the Lord's blessing absorbs all our energies [17].

65.10.0.en: b. A life of perpetual, everlasting joy and gladness [18-19], in which the voice of weeping or crying is not heard.

65.11.0.en: c. In it there is no one who bears the weakness of childhood or old age, but all enjoy spiritual maturity [20].

65.12.0.en: d. It is full of blessings: they build spiritual houses in which they dwell with God, and plant vineyards to be satisfied with the fruits of the Spirit [21].

65.13.0.en: e. The enemy (the devil) does not seize any place in them [23].

65.13.1.en: f. They are filled with peace, no terror comes upon them [13].

65.14.0.en: g. The Lord answers their prayers before they utter them: “And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear” [24].

65.14.1.en: h. A change of nature by the removal of the spirit of enmity and the enjoyment of the spirit of love and unity, even between the wolf and the lamb, the lion and the ox, the serpent and man! People come from diverse nations, some of them marked by ferocity, and all become one people under the leadership of the Spirit of the Holy God.

66.0.0.en: 1 Thus saith the LORD, “The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest? 2 For all those things hath mine hand made, and all those things have been, saith the LORD: but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word. 3 He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol. Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations. 4 I also will choose their calamities, and will bring their fears upon them; because when I called, none did answer; when I spake, they did not hear: but they did evil before mine eyes, and chose that in which I delighted not.”

66.0.1.en: The Jews often relied on the presence of the temple in Jerusalem as a source of security for them, whatever their life or their relationship with the Lord might be. Therefore the Lord rebukes them, saying: “The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest?” [1].

66.0.2.en: If God in His love for man permitted a house to be built for Him, it was only as a condescension of God to declare His dwelling in our midst. God is not concerned with stones and massive buildings; He dwells in “him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word” [see 2]. Solomon the wise realized this truth, and so he prayed on the day of the dedication of the temple, saying: “But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?” (1 Kgs 8:27).

66.0.3.en: * He truly accepted the temple that was called “the temple of Jerusalem” as a house for Himself or a dwelling place, not out of need of it but so that, as you look at it, you may offer your souls to Him.

66.0.4.en: St. Justin * What is this dwelling that David remembers and pours out his soul upon it (Ps 42:2), longing for this house in a love strong unto death? Is it the tabernacle made of skins and reeds and blue and purple?! Without doubt David's vision is quite different from that...

66.0.5.en: Put away from you every earthly thought, and come, walk in the way that the prophets and Apostles open for you, and above all walk in the Word of God with all your heart and with all your understanding, that you may ascend to heaven and contemplate the splendor of the eternal dwelling, of which Moses showed you only a shadow.

66.0.6.en: Origen * The Church of God is heaven!

66.0.7.en: * “The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom”... The righteous are the thrones.

66.0.8.en: * You have become a heaven; will you then fear the earth...?

66.0.9.en: Therefore when you have attained perfect knowledge and have love, you become the throne of God and a heaven. For this heaven that we look at with these eyes is not very precious before God. Our holy souls are God's heaven; the minds of the angels and of all the ministers are God's heaven.

66.1.0.en: St. Augustine The Church is entering into the rock, as the prophet Moses did in order to see the glory of God; this rock is Christ. We are established in Him in a spirit of humility with contrition, and so we enjoy the divine indwelling; therefore it was said: “But to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word” [2].

66.1.1.en: * Do you wish to be a place for the Lord? Be poor in spirit, contrite and trembling at the Word of God, and what you ask will be fulfilled for you.

66.1.2.en: * Let our hearts tremble when God looks upon us, and so He rests in them.

66.1.3.en: St. Augustine * Let us tremble at His words, that He may build us up always.

66.1.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * It is fitting for us to take care to be in the narrow, straight way, the way of praise and glory, where it is fitting for all Christians to practice peace, humility and the quietness of a good life according to the word of the Lord, who looks only to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at His word [2].

66.2.0.en: St. Cyprian Thus by humility, contrition of heart and fear of His words the Lord looks upon us, and dwells in us, and transforms us into His holy heavens. But whoever is occupied with formalities in worship in a spirit of hypocrisy and pride, God finds no rest in him, and his worship becomes an abomination before Him. God smells in the sacrifices the odor of murder, uncleanness and idol worship, for He says: “He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol” [3]. And as the wise man says: “The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD: but the prayer of the upright is his delight” (Prov 15:8).

66.2.1.en: * (Animal) sacrifices do not sanctify man, for God has no need of a sacrifice, but it is the conscience of the one who offers it that sanctifies the sacrifice when it is pure, and by this he moves God to accept the offering.

66.2.2.en: St. Irenaeus The fruit of being occupied with formalities without spirit is to enter into troubles without consolation; and instead of the Lord reassuring them by saying to each one of them: “Fear not: for I am with thee; I have called thee by thy name, thou art mine” (Isa 43:1), He says to them: “They have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations. I also will choose their calamities, and will bring their fears upon them; because when I called, none did answer; when I spake, they did not hear: but they did evil before mine eyes, and chose that in which I delighted not” [3-4].

66.2.3.en: They choose the evil way and delight in the abominations hated by the Lord; therefore God leaves them to their choice, and they fall under calamities that He brings upon them... which are the natural fruit of their conduct. They reject His call and do not listen to His voice; therefore He does not listen to their prayers nor answer their requests. They drink from the very cup that they filled.

66.3.s.en: 2. The distinction between the formalists and the earnest in worship:

66.3.0.en: 5 Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word: “Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed. 6 A voice of noise from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that rendereth recompence to his enemies. 7 Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. 8 Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children. 9 Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith the LORD: shall I cause to bring forth, and shut the womb? saith thy God.”

66.3.1.en: If the formalists in worship suffer troubles without consolation, then, on the contrary, those who are earnest in their lives, who tremble at the word of the Lord, are exposed to persecution even to expulsion, yet they enjoy true joy.

66.3.2.en: “Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word: Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed” [5]. This is what happened when the Jews hated the disciples of the Lord and His Apostles and cast them out under the cover of zeal for the glory of God and the Law of Moses, but the disciples rejoiced and their persecutors were put to shame. The Lord Christ pointed to this by saying: “They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service” (Jn 16:2).

66.4.0.en: As for the fruit of the affliction that came upon the men of the Church of the New Testament from their brethren, it is the destruction of the temple at the hands of Titus, for it was said here: “A voice of noise from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that rendereth recompence to his enemies” [6].

66.5.0.en: The opposition ended with the destruction of the temple, but the temple of the Church of the New Testament was established in every heart that bears fruit, which is the manifestation of the Lord of glory Jesus in the inner life of every believer. The prophet speaks to us here of the rise of this Church in a surpassing way, saying: “Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things?” [7-8]. What is this birth but the manifestation of the Lord Christ in the lives of the believers.

66.5.1.en: The Fathers of the Church look at the spiritual life of the Christian after his baptism as a state of growth of Christ Himself within their hearts, which are marked by motherhood toward Him.

66.5.2.en: * As the child is formed in the womb, so it seems to me that the Word of God is formed in the heart of the soul that has received the grace of Baptism, so that it perceives within it the word of faith more glorious and more clear.

66.5.3.en: * It seems wrong to speak of the Incarnation of the Son of God from the holy Virgin and not to point also to His incarnation in the Church... for it is fitting for each one of us to know the coming of the Son of God in the flesh by means of the pure Virgin, and at the same time to realize His coming in the Spirit in each one of us.

66.5.4.en: Origen * What happened to Mary, who was without blemish, when the fullness of the divinity that is in Christ shone in her, is realized in every soul that practices virginity as its rule. Truly the Lord no longer comes to dwell in a bodily dwelling, “yet now henceforth know we him no more” according to the flesh (2 Cor 5:6), but He dwells in us spiritually, and brings with Him His Father, as He told us in the Gospel...

66.5.5.en: * By this every Christian can become a mother of Him who is in essence everything, for our Lord Himself says: “Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my mother” (Mk 3:25; Mt 12:5).

66.5.6.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * (Every Christian) conceives God in his heart.

66.5.7.en: St. Augustine * He calls the soul that begins to move toward the Lord Christ thus: “Mary,” that is, it receives the name of the woman who bore Him in her womb, since the soul bears Him in a spiritual sense.

66.5.8.en: * Take care to fulfill the will of the Father so that you may be a mother of Christ (Mk 3:25).

66.6.0.en: St. Ambrose The catholic Church was born with power as in one day, for it was said: “Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once?” [8], since she was born on the day of Pentecost and grew with wonderful speed.

66.7.0.en: 10 Rejoice ye with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, all ye that love her: rejoice for joy with her, all ye that mourn for her: 11 That ye may suck, and be satisfied with the breasts of her consolations; that ye may milk out, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory. 12 For thus saith the LORD, “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream: then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees. 13 As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem. 14 And when ye see this, your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like an herb: and the hand of the LORD shall be known toward his servants, and his indignation toward his enemies. 15 For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. 16 For by fire and by his sword will the LORD plead with all flesh: and the slain of the LORD shall be many. 17 They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD. 18 And I will recompense their works and their thoughts: it shall come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory. 19 And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles. 20 And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, saith the LORD, as the children of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD. 21 And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD. 22 For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain. 23 And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD. 24 And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.”

66.7.1.en: The prophet concludes his discourse by revealing the new Jerusalem:

66.7.2.en: a. She overflows with joy and gladness upon those who love her and mourn for her because of the afflictions she suffers [10]. Outwardly there are pains and troubles, and inwardly an overflow of joy even upon others.

66.7.3.en: b. She overflows with satisfaction for all; she gives the little ones consolations as from the milk of her breasts, while she gives the grown the juice and delight of the abundance of her glory.

66.8.0.en: c. An overflow of peace like a river, and great glory like a flowing stream. “For thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream: then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees” [12].

66.8.1.en: God Himself directs peace upon His Church as the farmer waters his field, irrigating it from the springs of His peace as from an unfailing river, and pours glory out upon her.

66.8.2.en: * In His promise to the righteous He says that He will pour out upon them a river of peace, meaning that He will pour out upon them the greatest possibility. By this peace we are refreshed... and all are satisfied by it, for it will overflow even upon earthly bodies with the peace of incorruption and immortality... as though God pours (Himself) from the things above into the things below, and makes men equal to the angels.

66.9.0.en: St. Augustine d. A source of divine comfort: “As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem” [13]. God, as Father, grants the Church a motherhood not only toward the believers, her children, but toward every human being; she bears a heart as wide as her Bridegroom's, to overflow with love upon all.

66.9.1.en: As a mother she offers comfort to her children, especially those who suffer and bear the cross; this comfort is not from her own resources, but is the gift of the Holy Spirit who dwells in her... therefore the Lord says, “so will I comfort you” [3].

66.9.2.en: As for the men of the Old Testament, they found their comfort in Jerusalem in two respects: that they had returned from captivity, and that God dwells in their midst. But in the New Testament the Holy Spirit gives us His consolations in victory over the enemy who shatters our freedom, and in our being accepted as a dwelling for the Holy Trinity.

66.10.0.en: “And when ye see this, your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like an herb: and the hand of the LORD shall be known toward his servants, and his indignation toward his enemies” [14]. We see the Cross, for in it life appeared, and the hand of the Lord is known, that is, the person of the Lord Christ is revealed as the hand of the Father... for by Him the love of God the Father was practically accomplished through the sacrifice of the Cross. In the Church we enjoy this, so our hearts rejoice with gladness, and the bones of our faith flourish. This is our comfort in the Lord through His Church: He gives us the joy of the heavenly heart and its enlargement with love, and He causes our faith to grow (the bones being the center of the body).

66.11.0.en: e. A source of purity: “They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD” [17]; “as the children of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD” [20].

66.12.0.en: f. She declares the glory of God among the Gentiles [18-20].

66.13.0.en: g. A priestly city: “And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD” [21].

66.14.0.en: h. An eternal city: “so shall your seed and your name remain” [22].

66.15.0.en: i. A people perpetually in worship: “And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD” [23].

66.16.0.en: j. Among them there is no one perishing... rather, perdition is accomplished outside the true Jerusalem. “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh” [24].
